''"A deadly huntress from the foglands. Eradicates foes with daggers and poisons."'' {{Icon|}}
 The '''Silent '''is one of four playable characters in Slay the Spire. She is a huntress themed on a rogue fantasy build. The Silent weakens her foes with numerous cuts and poison, while using cheap tricks and agility to avoid their attacks. With many powerful cards that draw and discard, the Silent ensures that she will always be one step ahead of her enemy. She has the lowest starting health of any character, at 70 hp.   The Silent's starting [[Relic]] is {{R|Ring of the Snake}}, which draws 2 additional cards at the start of combat.  ==Cards== ===Starting Deck=== *  5 {{C|Strike_G|Strikes}} *  5 {{C|Defend_G|Defends}} *  1 {{C|Survivor}} *  1 {{C|Neutralize}}
{{Silent Card Navbox}} == Relics== Starting Relic: {{R|Ring of the Snake}} Common Relic: {{R|Snecko Skull}} Uncommon Relics: {{R|Ninja Scroll}}, {{R|Paper Krane}} Rare Relics: {{R|The Specimen}}, {{R|Tingsha}}, {{R|Tough Bandages}} Boss Relics: {{R|Hovering Kite}}, {{R|Ring of the Serpent}} (replaces {{R|Ring of the Snake}}), {{R|Wrist Blade}} Shop Relic: {{R|Twisted Funnel}} ==Strategy== The Silent does not have any reliable ability to heal or gain an abundance of starting health. Therefore, she is often focused on preventing damage by combining and chaining {{KW|Block}} and {{KW|Weak}}, and then steadily building advantage over enemies to end the encounter at opportune times. Many of her cards draw cards, discard cards, reduce costs, or give additional {{KW|Energy}}, allowing her to overcome the low impact of individual cards by taking advantage of a properly built deck's synergies. ===Starting Deck & Relic=== The Silent's starting deck is the largest of all the characters at 12 cards, compared to 10 cards in the Ironclad's, Defect's, and Watcher's starting decks. This means more Strikes and Defends are encountered in Act 1, and it's slightly more difficult to remove all starting cards from The Silent's Deck. The Silent's starting deck is also the cheapest, with its 2 additional cards {{C|Survivor}} and {{C|Neutralize}}, costing 1 and 0, respectively. This makes it somewhat more viable to select more 2-cost cards earlier in the game, such as {{C|Dash}}, {{C|Predator}}, or {{C|Leg Sweep}}. Her starting Relic, {{R|Ring of the Snake}}, ensures that the player has more options for choosing which cards to play on the first turn of every fight. The extra 2 cards drawn can mitigate the slight drawback of {{KW|Innate}} cards, since, with the Silent, the Innate card replaces only 1 of the 7 cards drawn at the start of combat, rather than 1 of the 5 cards drawn with the other characters. (I.e., if the player has the Ring of the Snake relic in their inventory and one Innate card in their deck, they will start combat with that Innate card while drawing 6 random cards, whereas other characters with one Innate card in their deck will draw only 4 random cards at the start of each combat). The "Bottle Relics" ({{R|Bottled Flame}}, {{R|Bottled Lightning}}, and {{R|Bottled Tornado}}) have similar utility for the same reason. Owing to these properties, the Silent's early-game performance is by far the weakest out of the four characters. Her lack of access to immediate damage leaves her ill-equipped to deal with the Act 1 Elite encounters, particularly [[Lagavulin]] and [[Gremlin Nob]], if players do not select cards to increase the damage density of her deck. Because of this, even getting a Silent run started can be difficult, particularly on high [[Ascension]] levels. However, if players can overcome the early-game hurdle and build a synergistic deck, they can make use of the Silent's incredible late-game potential where her performance is arguably, on average, the strongest of the four characters. Her cards can provide access to some of the strongest damage mitigation in the game, highly advantageous card manipulation, and damage outputs that are consistent and can scale with late-game enemies. In this way, a player using the Silent can create decks that may seem weak in the early Acts, but that can complete the Act 3 boss gauntlet and the [[Corrupt Heart]] with correct play. ===Synergies=== Listed below are the standard synergies that Silent decks build towards, which may provide you with direction for your own runs. There are some important things to keep in mind while evaluating these synergies: *Most of these builds aren't mutually exclusive. Each of the archetypes listed below can be thought of as an engine that you can incorporate into your deck; and, depending on the situation, you can plausibly adapt or combine multiple archetypes into a single strategy. :*In particular, the different aspects of Silent's strategies can organically mesh with each other (e.g., high defense cards can combine with slow-building poison cards to consistently prevent damage while steadily chipping away at enemy health). Keep synergies in mind, but don't always turn down individually powerful cards just because they may not match a synergy that you currently have or are planning around. *It's important to not "force" a particular build from the outset of the game. The priority in selecting cards and working towards a build should be to solve your immediate problems, while allowing an archetype to come to you more naturally. The only exception would be if you run into cards or relics in the early-game that are both individually impactful ''and'' form the crux of an entire archetype, and such situations are rare. ==== General ==== Cards that are generally good in any Silent strategy include: *{{C|Well-Laid Plans}}. The ability to hold key cards for when you need them most is highly impactful and contributes to the Silent's late-game strengths. For example, you can hold onto the crucial {{C|Burst}} + {{C|Catalyst}} combo until you've stacked a critical value of of {{KW|Poison}}, or wait to play {{C|Wraith Form}} until an enemy's most powerful hits, etc. Even outside of these examples, simply holding over damage or block on a turn where you don't need either one ''quite yet'' can deal with whatever the enemy throws at you. *{{C|Alchemize}}. [[Potions]] are an incredibly strong resource in ''Slay the Spire'', especially as you unlock higher [[Ascension]] levels, because they can be used whenever you need them, or saved for difficult fights. So, a card like {{C|Alchemize}} makes almost every deck stronger, since it gives you access to [[Potions]] outside of combat-rewards. {{Archetype|[[Discard]] & Draw |text=While {{KW|Poison}} and {{C|Shiv}} synergies usually capture the attention of new ''Spire'' players, Silent's biggest strength is arguably her card manipulation, much of which owes to her ability to cycle through the deck effortlessly. Her [[discard]] and card draw effects are thus the bread-and-butter of many of the strongest Silent decks, allowing unparalleled consistency in executing the deck's win condition. Cards that provide card draw: *{{C|Acrobatics}} is Silent's main cycling tool, allowing you to see 3 (4) new cards from your deck at a low cost, and even allows you to trigger discard synergies, all on a Common! *{{C|Tools of the Trade}} allows you to see an extra card every turn. *{{C|Backflip}} draws 2 while providing a small amount of {{KW|Block}}. If your late-game Block plan involves stacking {{KW|Dexterity}}, this can provide an incredible amount of incidental Block for you while you look for your key cards. *{{C|Prepared}} is nothing special unupgraded, as it merely replaces itself. However, Prepared+ is a very strong tool that allows you to dig further through your deck for free. *{{C|Calculated Gamble}} allows you to see an entire new hand, and when upgraded, no longer Exhausts, meaning you can do this every cycle. *{{C|Expertise}} is by far the weakest out of Silent's card draw tools, as it is conditional, and she wants to keep a large hand anyway. However, if you have no other sources of draw that increase your hand size, it will do in a pinch. Cards that benefit off discards: *{{C|Eviscerate}} is a premium frontloaded damage option for a deck that cycles a lot. It will frequently cost nothing and slam an enemy for a good chunk of damage, and synergizes well with any source of {{KW|Strength}} or even {{R|Wrist Blade}} if fully discounted. *{{C|Sneaky Strike}} refunds itself if you've discarded anything during the turn. By itself, it's a decent damage button for the early-game that retains some value later on. Later on, if you find any way to discount it (such as with the otherwise niche {{C|Setup}}), it can even become an {{KW|Energy}} generator! *{{C|Concentrate}} gives a huge burst of {{KW|Energy}} for decks that have a surplus of draw but not enough Energy generation. It becomes absolutely broken with {{R|Runic Pyramid}}, as you will almost be guaranteed to have a full hand, and Concentrate will make hand space for you to continue your turn. *{{C|Tactician}} grants 1 (2) {{KW|Energy}} when discarded. If your deck can reliably discard {{C|Tactician}}, then it has a steady supply of {{KW|Energy}}, which makes most of your turns much more efficient. With a small enough deck, you can actually guarantee discarding {{C|Tactician}} multiple times, which can become infinite. *{{C|Reflex}} draws 2 (3) cards when discarded. While not as crucial in a deck with a lot of Backflips and Acrobatics, it still has a strong place in Silent's kit. A fully upgraded {{C|Reflex}} combined with {{C|Prepared}}, upgraded {{C|Calculated Gamble}}, and a small deck can go infinite. While Silent's card draw power is usually in service of her other synergies, discard can occasionally be a win condition all by itself. The aforementioned infinites are one aveune for that, but these are some others: *{{R|Tingsha}}/{{R|Tough Bandages}} deals 3 damage / grants 3 block on each discard. If you can get these relics, you can simply spam discard to fight for you without even having to play output cards! *{{C|Phantasmal Killer}} can be your entire damage solve, as if you cycle enough, you can end up playing it on every single turn, removing the need to line it up carefully. Slamming the enemy with double damage Eviscerates and Sneaky Strikes can sometimes be enough even in the absence of traditional scaling. *{{C|Grand Finale}}, while often niche, has its best showing in particularly discard- and draw-heavy decks, especially if you have {{R|Runic Pyramid}}. Because you can control how much you draw every turn, with enough careful planning, you can get the Finale off with reasonable consistency. }} ==== Offensive ==== {{Archetype|{{KW|Poison}} |text={{KW|Poison}} Builds use {{KW|Poison}} stacks as their main source of damage. With the right cards, you can ramp up {{KW|Poison}} stacks on an enemy very quickly and kill them in 1-2 turns. However, the usual style of {{KW|Poison}} builds slowly ramp up stacks over time and whittle the enemy down over many turns. *{{C|Noxious Fumes}}, on its own, will gradually build up more and more poison until the enemy dies. It allows many builds to play much more defensively, and stall out fights with full-defense turns, as they are passively dealing more and more damage. Synergizes amazingly with {{KW|Block}} Builds. However, this playstyle struggles with enemies that scale by buffing their own strength. {{C|Malaise}} is a great addition to a {{C|Noxious Fumes|Fumes}} build. *{{C|Poisoned Stab}} is a decent damage source on its own, which becomes better when you have a {{KW|Poison}} deck and can reliably stack {{KW|Poison}}. *{{C|Catalyst}}, if you're able to play it multiple times, can exponentially increase {{KW|Poison}} to ridiculous levels in a single turn. With {{C|Nightmare}} or {{C|Burst}} (or both), you get extra plays out of your {{C|Catalyst}}, which can quickly stack up hundreds of {{KW|Poison}}. This build has incredible single-target damage, but is very bad at damaging multiple targets (without {{R|The Specimen}}), and requires a decent supply of draw/energy. Very good for all single-target encounters, and becomes worse the more enemies there are. *Average {{KW|Poison}} cards are not that great on their own, and only become stronger if you already have a {{KW|Poison}} deck built around them. **{{C|Bane}} **{{C|Deadly Poison}} **{{C|Bouncing Flask}} **{{C|Crippling Cloud}} *{{C|Envenom}} adds {{KW|Poison}} onto all of your attack cards. Works extremely well if you are able to play many attack cards in a turn. Synergizes well with cheap attacks like {{C|Endless Agony}}, multiple-hit attacks like {{C|Riddle with Holes}}, {{C|Finisher}}, and {{C|Eviscerate}}, and pretty much all {{C|Shiv}}-generating cards. *{{C|Corpse Explosion}} could help solve the lack of AoE damage of {{KW|Poison}}. *{{R|Snecko Skull}} is very strong for poison decks; it simply just gives more poison to your existing poison cards. You get the best value from this using poison sources that give small stacks of poison at a time: namely, {{C|Noxious Fumes}} and {{C|Envenom}}. It also works well with {{C|Bouncing Flask}}, since it applies poison multiple times. *{{R|The Specimen}} gives poison decks much-needed multi-target damage. This is a must-have if you encounter this relic and have committed to making a poison deck. *If possible getting a {{C|Sadistic Nature}} this type of deck will work wonders for the lack of upfront damage. }} {{Archetype|{{C|Shiv}} Deck |text=A primarily damage-focused build that revolves around gaining and using many {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} during each combat. The Silent also has a few [[Relics]] that are specifically for enhancing Shivs. *{{C|Infinite Blades}}, {{C|Cloak and Dagger}}, and {{C|Blade Dance}} are absolute musts for the archetype. All add {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} to your hand. Amplified by strength cards and relics (i.e. {{C|J.A.X.}}, {{R|Shuriken}}, {{R|Kunai}}, {{R|Ornamental Fan}}). Don't forget to upgrade {{C|Infinite Blades}} first so it appears innately in your hand. *{{R|Wrist Blade}} amplifies not only {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} but Silent's other 0 energy attacks, such as {{C|Slice}} and {{C|Backstab}}. 0 energy attacks also have great synergy with {{C|Choke}} and {{C|A Thousand Cuts}}. *{{R|Ninja Scroll}} can quickly jump start your first turn every combat. *{{C|Accuracy}} amplifies your shivs. The more, the better. Beware of [[Awakened One|The Awakened One]]. *{{C|Envenom}} applies {{KW|Poison}} while you attack with barrages of {{C|Shiv|Shivs}}. Couple with the {{R|Snecko Skull}} relic for easy clears.{{C|Sadistic Nature}} also combines extremely effectively with it; the {{KW|Poison}} from {{C|Envenom}} will trigger the damage from {{C|Sadistic Nature}}. This strategy can serve as a bridge between {{KW|Poison}} and {{C|Shiv}} builds in case you end up with a mix of cards and relics suitable for each. **{{C|Storm of Steel}} can be a great finisher if you have {{C|Envenom}}. *A couple of {{C|After Image|After Images}} give you great survivability due to card-spamming nature of this archetype. *After unloading all your {{C|Shiv|Shivs}}, {{C|Finisher}} adds free damage. *{{R|Dead Branch}} - {{C|Shiv|Shivs}} {{KW|exhaust}} when played, and so benefit from relics that trigger on card {{KW|exhaust|exhaustion}}. *{{R|Anchor}} is useful for surviving while setting up your combo since your initial setup will take up most of your energy ({{C|Infinite Blades}}, {{C|After Image}}, {{C|A Thousand Cuts}}, etc.) *{{C|A Thousand Cuts}} provides a good AoE damage for this deck. *{{C|Choke}} offers strong single-target damage in a {{C|Shiv}} deck. Also, since {{C|Choke}} causes the target to lose life instead of taking damage, it bypasses enemy {{KW|Block}}. *{{C|Expertise}} is very good for refilling your hand after playing your low-cost {{C|Shiv}}/{{C|Slice}}/{{C|Endless Agony}} cards. *Since you will be playing a lot of {{C|Shiv}}, which is an [[Attack]], you will trigger relics like {{R|Ornamental Fan}}, {{R|Nunchaku}}, {{R|Kunai}}, and {{R|Shuriken}} many times. *Shiv decks struggle against [[Time Eater]] (because shiv decks rely on playing large volumes of cards) and [[Corrupt Heart]] (because of Beat of Death), so have a plan to account for those. [[Envenom]] can help by adding passive damage to each shiv. {{R|Tungsten Rod}} can mitigate Beat of Death entirely if the run is at low enough Ascension or if the player has {{R|Torii}} as well. ** Beat of Death can also be mitigated with 2 {{C|After Image|After Images}} (3 on [[Ascension]] 19+) }} ==== Defensive ==== {{Archetype|{{KW|Dexterity}} Stacking + {{KW|Weak}} Chain |text=Silent's base {{KW|Block}} numbers are quite low, but her access to {{KW|Dexterity}} through {{C|Footwork}}, her ability to play many cards per turn, and her many cards that can keep {{KW|Weak}} onto enemies, all prop up how low those numbers are. This can be a powerful late-game defense solution as the package is quite lightweight, yet can stall out combats effectively until the deck's main damage engine comes online. Sources of {{KW|Dexterity}}: *{{C|Footwork}}, which gives you 2 (3) {{KW|Dexterity}} for the rest of the combat. One or two copies can be enough, but it never hurts to include more — as many as you're able to without harming the consistency of your first cycle through the deck. *{{R|Kunai}}, which gives you 1 {{KW|Dexterity}} every time you play 3 Attacks in a single turn. This synergizes beautifully with {{C|Shiv}}-generating cards, which basically turn into Dexterity generators while also dealing damage. If you find this relic early and lean into Shivs, you might not even need Footworks! {{C|Cloak and Dagger}} becomes particularly good with this relic. *{{R|Oddly Smooth Stone}}, which benefits all characters would be the cornerstone for easy dexterity especially if you have Footwork. Sources of {{KW|Weak}}: *{{C|Neutralize}}+ *{{C|Sucker Punch}}+ *{{C|Crippling Cloud}} is AoE {{KW|Weak}} that can mitigate a large amount of damage while providing some {{KW|Poison}} ticks. *{{C|Leg Sweep}} is a card that provides both {{KW|Weak}} and {{KW|Block}} at the same time. It doesn't benefit as much from {{KW|Dexterity}} due to its high cost, but excels in stopping single-target damage. Block cards that benefit most from the accumulated {{KW|Dexterity}}: *{{C|Backflip}} is not only a good draw card but, as mentioned in the previous section, can incidentally generate lots of {{KW|Block}} while helping you cycle if you have ample Dexterity. *{{C|Deflect}} goes from being relatively low-impact to potentially blocking for double-digit numbers for 0 {{KW|Energy}} once you've put all the Footworks down, making it a good inclusion, particularly if you have lots of draw to find it consistently. *{{C|Dodge and Roll}} scales with {{KW|Dexterity}} twice, and gets extra value when you know you will be attacked every turn. *{{C|Blur}} is very good at stacking {{KW|Block}} over multiple turns if you find yourself frequently overblocking. However, it's not as consistent as [[Ironclad]]'s {{C|Barricade}} at doing so, since it only lasts one turn. You need to use it wisely or have multiple copies of Blur if you are reliant on this for critical turns in the endgame. Other considerations: *{{C|Burst}} is another strong card, as it basically doubles the {{KW|Block}} of your next {{KW|Block}} card (or ''two'' when upgraded!) It goes very well with all the above {{KW|Block}} cards, especially {{C|Dodge and Roll}} and {{C|Blur}}, and is generally a strong card for turning on your damage engine as well. *Base {{C|Defend}} cards are actually quite strong with these types of synergies, and shouldn't be removed from the deck. If you identify that this will be your main defense solve, consider taking '''[Simplicity]''' at [[Ancient Writing]] to upgrade them to bolster your base numbers even further. It's also one of the clearest applications of accepting {{R|Mark of the Bloom}} by taking '''[I Am Awake]''' at [[Mind Bloom]], because it will also upgrade all of the other {{KW|Block}} cards you've added to your deck alongside any Footworks that haven't been upgraded, which can result in you taking no damage for the rest of the run. *{{R|Paper Krane}} amplifies the effectiveness of your {{KW|Weak}} from 25% to 40%. Due to how rounding in ''Spire'' works, this can mitigate a lot more damage than you expect, so definitely take advantage of this relic if you find it. *{{C|Sadistic Nature}} works with the weak chaining providing the needed passive damage. }} {{Archetype|Non-{{KW|Dexterity}} Mitigation |text=The Silent also has a bevy of damage mitigation options to choose from that don't involve {{KW|Dexterity}}. *{{C|Piercing Wail}} is perhaps the best example of this. It's a Common card that takes away 6 (8) {{KW|Strength}} from enemies for that turn — it completely shuts down multi-hits, notably completely blocking the [[Corrupt Heart]]'s Blood Shots all the way into the ''third'' cycle, and can control multi-enemy encounters, all for just 1 {{KW|Energy}}. For multi-stage boss fights such as the [[Awakened One]] or [[Time Eater]], playing Piercing Wail on the turn they "reset" (before you kill the first phase of the Awakened One, or on the turn that Time Eater clears debuffs and heals back to half) will cause them to permanently lose that much Strength. Every deck benefits from at least a few copies of Piercing Wail. *{{C|Malaise}} is one of the strongest cards in Silent's card pool, being able to not only keep {{KW|Weak}} on an enemy but also permanently reduce their {{KW|Strength}}, neutering multi-hits in the process. It is one of the very best solutions to [[Time Eater]] in particular, and can buy enough time for {{C|Shiv}} strategies to scale without fearing giving the boss too much {{KW|Strength}}. *{{C|After Image}} is a very good {{KW|Block}} card with huge value throughout every combat. For 1 {{KW|Energy}}, you get usually at least 4-5 block every turn for the rest of combat. It synergizes very well with card-generation cards and 0-{{KW|Energy}} cards, and goes particularly well into {{C|Shiv}} strategies. *{{C|Wraith Form}} is one of the most powerful individual cards in the game, giving you {{KW|Intangible}} for 2 (3) turns. Often times, this is enough time to straight-up end hallway fights because you can now focus all of your {{KW|Energy}} on attacking without much fear of taking damage. If you have multiple copies of Wraith Form or a way to duplicate it (such as with {{C|Nightmare}}), {{C|After Image}} to block chip damage, or {{R|Orange Pellets}} to erase the {{KW|Dexterity}}-down debuff, you can even ignore its downside completely. On [[Ascension]] 19 and 20, it also lowers the [[Corrupt Heart]]'s {{KW|Beat of Death}} damage down from 2 or 3 to 1. Other considerations: *{{C|Nightmare}} can be a difficult card to pick, but with enough card manipulation and the correct targets (most of which are defensive), it can provide an out to every fight in the game. It is best with cards listed in this section, such as Malaise, After Image, and Wraith Form, as they all become significantly stronger in multiples. However, it can also be used to duplicate {{C|Footwork}} as well, in case you don't have enough for a particular fight. Two copies of Nightmare (one used to duplicate the other) can allow you to duplicate cards indefinitely, so long as you have the {{KW|Energy}} for it. Nightmare can also duplicate {{C|Alchemize}} to increase your chances of finding strong Potions, most notably [[Ghost in a Jar]] which is a free turn of {{KW|Intangible}}. }} ==Unlocks== The Silent is unlocked by completing a run with The Ironclad. {| class="article-table" !Unlock Number !Prizes Unlocked |- |1st |{{C|Bane}}, {{C|Catalyst}}, {{C|Corpse Explosion}} |- |2nd |{{R|Du-Vu Doll}}, {{R|Smiling Mask}}, {{R|Tiny Chest}} |- |3rd |{{C|Cloak and Dagger}}, {{C|Accuracy}}, {{C|Storm of Steel}} |- |4th |{{R|Art of War}}, {{R|The Courier}}, {{R|Pandora's Box}} |- |5th |{{C|Concentrate}}, {{C|Setup}}, {{C|Grand Finale}} |} == Gallery== soylent1.jpg|The Silent in-game soylent2.jpg|The Silent appearing in her Steam Background soylent3.png|The Silent featured prominently in the card art for [[Die Die Die]] Chad4.jpg|The Silent appearing alongside the [[Ironclad]] in official game art soylent4.JPG|The Silent's character select screen chad6.jpg|The Silent alongside the [[Ironclad]] in official game artwork Gallerypiece.JPG|The Silent seen in the Launch Trailer alongside the [[Ironclad]] and the [[Defect]] [[Category:Class]]
